rationale: Successor execution of the restart/durable-vote discriminator, changing the basis that made the previous run inapplicable: the target is isolated from its real peers before any probe and reached only through a dedicated probe transport connected to the target's own transport, and the post-restart probes are issued immediately so they fall inside the target's election-timer window; each probe reports both the granted flag and whether it was actually delivered, and the harness emits an explicit applicability flag (restored currentTerm equals the probe term and the durable LastVoteTerm equals the probe term) so an inapplicable run is visible rather than being read as a denial. Previous execution 79eba5e015d84914afd69dac65a62430-experiment was unresolved because the target stayed a live cluster member whose peers advanced its term past the probe term; this revision keeps the same investigation and observable endpoint but removes that producer of term change. The harness compiles against the snapshot (go vet clean in the local fixed-input workspace).

experiment.revision_reason: The previous execution could not exercise the same-term duplicate rule: the target remained a live voter whose real peers advanced its term past the probe term after it accepted a future-term vote, so all post-restart probes were decided by the older-term rule. This revision isolates the target from its peers and probes immediately after the restart within the election-timer window.

scope.description: One process: three real raft instances are bootstrapped (MakeCluster(3)) and then the target is isolated from the other two with the cluster's transport-level Disconnect. A dedicated InmemTransport is connected only to the target's transport and is used for every probe. A RequestVote for candidate A in term target.getCurrentTerm()+5 is delivered into the target's consumer and the granted flag plus the durable LastVoteTerm/LastVoteCand keys are recorded. The target is then shut down and rebuilt over the same log/stable/snapshot stores, FSM and transport; immediately afterwards the restored currentTerm and durable vote keys are recorded with an applicability flag, and three probes are issued inside the election-timer window: the same candidate in the same term, a different candidate in the same term, and a different candidate in an older term.

experiment.prefix: MakeCluster(3) bootstraps three Voters over InmemTransport and waits for a leader, so both candidate IDs are Voters in the target's latest configuration; the target is raft 2, and the candidate IDs/addresses come from rafts 1 and 0. Isolation uses cluster.Disconnect on the target's address, which removes the target from every other transport's peer map and disconnects the target from them, without editing production source. Delivery is preserved because the probe transport is connected to the target's transport separately, so the target still receives RPCs while its real peers cannot advance its term. Every request sets RPCHeader{ProtocolVersion:3, ID: candidateID, Addr: encoded candidate} and takes LastLogIndex/LastLogTerm from the target's own last entry so the log-up-to-date rule grants, with LeadershipTransfer=true so the known-leader rule does not decide the outcome. After the restart the probes run with no sleep so they precede the fresh node's first heartbeat-timeout election; the harness emits restored currentTerm against the probe term and the durable vote term so applicability is checkable from the receipt alone.
